wi_east_bluff_05_potholes_area.blurb: This stretch of the East Bluff sits above Devil's Lake in the Baraboo Range, along the Potholes Trail where the path climbs through a narrow gap in the rock. The climbing is mostly traditional, with a smaller share of top-rope routes and almost no bouldering. Grades run from 5.2 to 5.12, with plenty of moderates between 5.4 and 5.8 and a short list of hard lines at the top. The park's cliffs are Baraboo quartzite, and the park has no permanent bolts or anchors, so leaders place removable gear while newer climbers usually top-rope. Ratings tend to feel stiff. Doorway Rocks, split into the Major Mass and the Minor Mass, holds the most climbs, followed by Ramsay's Pinnacle and Red Rock.

az_pima_canyon_area.blurb: Pima Canyon is a bouldering area inside South Mountain Park in Phoenix, split into eleven sub-areas of boulders and short walls. Nearly everything here is a boulder problem, and the grades cover a wide range: plenty of easy and mid-grade problems from V0 to V5, then a thinner tail of harder ones up to around V9. Several problems are overhanging. Rock quality is mixed, with the well-traveled problems generally sound and the less-visited ones calling for care. At the Entrance Boulders, the main wall has crumbly top-outs. World Boulder holds the most climbs, followed by the Entrance Boulders and The Amphitheatre, with Seven Samurai and Africa Boulder also holding sizeable groups.

ca_silver_lake.blurb: Silver Lake is a cluster of crags on the hillside above the June Lake Loop in the Eastern Sierra. The rock is quartzite, described as sound and compact, and most routes are easy to moderate, roughly 70 to 200 feet long. Nearly all of it is either bolted for sport leading or set up with top-rope anchors, with only a few trad lines. Grades run from 5.2 to 5.11, with most routes between 5.6 and 5.9. The cliffs face east-northeast, so they catch early sun on cool days and fall into shade late on hot ones. The rock has seen little climbing and some of it is still loose, so belayers should stand well clear. Moynier, Lewis and Franosch hold the most climbs.

co_piedra_river.blurb: The Piedra River climbing sits just north of Pagosa Springs, on cliffs above the river. Sport routes make up most of it, mixed in with trad lines, top-ropes, mixed climbs and a scattering of boulder problems that run from V0 to V7. The roped grades concentrate between 5.10 and 5.12, with a smaller number of 5.8 and 5.9 routes. Lower West holds the most climbs and has a creekside setting that gets morning sun in summer, and the East Side comes next. On the East Side the lower face is described as chossy. Poison ivy grows along the trails near the creek in summer.

va_atkins_bouldering.blurb: Atkins is a bouldering area on the south side of Big Walker Mountain in Southwest Virginia. Almost everything is a boulder problem, and grades run from V0 up to around V8, with the middle of the range, V3 to V5, holding the most problems. At Roadside Boulders the rock is sandstone with slopey holds and tough top-outs, and that area is described as a good fit for cool-weather trips. The Drop is a horseshoe-shaped band of short, highly featured sandstone cliff, with problems from tall slabs to long roofs and slopey top-outs. Springs keep the roof and lower cliff there wet from early spring to late summer, while most of its lines stay dry year-round.

az_central_mogollon_rim.blurb: Central Mogollon Rim is a set of canyons in Northern Arizona that cut down the basalt rim toward the Verde Valley. Trad dominates, with a good number of sport routes, a few boulder problems and some water ice. Roped grades run from 5.6 to 5.12, with 5.10 the biggest group, and the ice is WI4 to WI5. West Clear Creek holds the most climbs. It is a sandstone canyon with crack climbing, mostly trad, where bolts are sparse and widely spaced, and it is described as a good summer destination, roughly April through October. Thirteen Mile Rock is a basalt butte, and Wet Beaver Crack and Natural Spring round out the larger areas.
